prompt.context_jp: ようやく部屋を出ようとした矢先、玄関前で軽い足音___止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces this new, unexpected event?

feedback.correct_en: The footsteps are brand-new information appearing unexpectedly — が marks the newly introduced subject of an event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest the footsteps are already an established topic, which they aren't. で doesn't fit as subject marker.

contrast_examples.en: Footsteps stopped. [new event]
(As for) those footsteps, they stopped. [already known]

prompt.context_jp: 親父の3回忌なんだ 死んで2年なのに なんで3回忌っていうんだろうな
prompt.prompt_jp: 死んで2年なのに なんで3回忌っていうんだろう。「3回忌」___ 変な言い方だな。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces this new topic into the conversation?

feedback.correct_en: って introduces a term being commented on — 'this thing called 3回忌'. It fits raising a word as a topic in casual speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would require a transitive verb; に marks direction/time, not the thing being discussed.

contrast_examples.en: These things called ceremonies... [raising a topic]
Avoid ceremonies. [direct object]

prompt.context_jp: 信介にとって___、独り身の身の上を追及される避けようのない一時である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Shinsuke's perspective as the topic frame?

feedback.correct_en: にとっては sets Shinsuke's viewpoint as the topic frame — 'from Shinsuke's perspective, it is...'. は naturally follows にとって to establish a topical stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: にとってが is ungrammatical. も would imply 'also for Shinsuke', requiring a prior parallel referent.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼にとっては辛い時間だ。
contrast_examples.en: For him, it's a painful time. [topical frame]
For him too, it's painful. [addition]

prompt.context_jp: 桑野家を継ぐの___ 長男のあんただけなんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'the only one who inherits is you'?

feedback.correct_en: Here 継ぐのは〜だけ sets up a topic ('the one who inherits') and identifies the sole person. は works as topicalizer with the exhaustive 'only' predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would compete with the だけ-focus structure; the natural pattern pairs は with the nominalized subject phrase. を doesn't fit the の nominalization here.

contrast_examples.jp: 継ぐのはあんただけだ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who inherits is only you.
YOU are the one who inherits. [exhaustive が]

prompt.context_jp: 会う度に同じこと言ってるよ あの連中___
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — Shinsuke singling out 'those people' with a critical, contrastive tone?

feedback.correct_en: Postposed あの連中は carries contrastive/critical topic marking — 'those guys (as opposed to normal people) always say the same thing'. は fits the complaining tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just neutrally identify the subject without the contrastive bite. も would mean 'those guys too', implying others also do it — not the point here.

contrast_examples.jp: あの連中は、いつも同じだ。
contrast_examples.en: Those guys (contrastively) are always the same.
Those guys said it. [neutral identification]

prompt.context_jp: あなた___ 同じこと言わせているんでしょう？
prompt.prompt_en: Mother Ikuyo pushes back: 'YOU are the one making them say it.' Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively identifies 'you' as the real culprit — 'it's YOU who makes them say it'. Perfect for pointing back at the responsible party.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just topicalize 'you' without the accusatory focus. The rebuttal needs the pinpointing force of が.

contrast_examples.en: It's YOU who makes them say it. [identifying culprit]
As for you, you make them say it. [weak/topical]

prompt.context_jp: 結婚したら お前の親だけじゃないんだぞ 相手の親___いるんだぞ
prompt.prompt_en: Eiji reminds Shinsuke there ALSO exist in-laws. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: も adds 'the partner's parents too' to お前の親, highlighting that in-laws also exist alongside your own parents.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize without the 'also' nuance Eiji needs. が would just assert existence neutrally, losing the additive point about having TWO sets.

contrast_examples.en: There are also the partner's parents. [addition]
There are the partner's parents. [plain existence]

prompt.context_jp: その写真に 女の手___写ってるだろう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces 'a woman's hand' as newly noticed detail?

feedback.correct_en: The woman's hand is new, salient information being pointed out for the first time — が marks this newly-noticed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the hand is already a known topic. を would require a transitive verb; 写る is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: A hand is visible. [new detail]
That hand (known) is hers.

prompt.context_jp: 結婚相手___ ちゃんとした人なら その人のお母さんだって ちゃんとした人のはずでしょう
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the conditional 'if the marriage partner is a decent person'?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a なら conditional subordinate clause, the subject typically takes が rather than は, especially when stating a condition about an unspecified partner.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would pull the topic out of the conditional scope, creating awkward emphasis. を doesn't fit with だ-predicate.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手がちゃんとした人なら…
contrast_examples.en: If the partner is a decent person... [condition]

contrast_examples.jp: 相手はちゃんとした人だ。
contrast_examples.en: The partner is a decent person. [main clause topic]

prompt.context_jp: 抑える人___ いなくなって ますます頑固で口うるさくなって
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the person who held him back' in this subordinate clause?

feedback.correct_en: Within the subordinate 〜なって clause describing a new circumstance (the restrainer being gone), が marks the subject of the event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize across the subordinate boundary, which is unnatural here. も would add 'also', which isn't the meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 抑える人がいなくなった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who restrained him disappeared. [event]

contrast_examples.jp: あの人はいなくなった。
contrast_examples.en: As for him, he's gone. [topical]

prompt.context_jp: お前___ お父さんの話を 聞こうとしないから この人に頼んで 呼び出してもらったんだ
prompt.prompt_en: Yasuo scolds Natsumi. Which particle fits 'because YOU won't listen'?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a から causal subordinate clause, the subject naturally takes が. It also carries a pointed 'it's YOU who won't listen' feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would shift to topicalization, which is less natural inside a tight causal clause pinpointing blame.

contrast_examples.jp: お前が聞かないから困る。
contrast_examples.en: Because YOU don't listen, I'm in trouble.
You are someone who doesn't listen. [main clause topic]

prompt.context_jp: 何しろ 財布のヒモを 握ってんの___ お父さまだから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in '(the one) who holds the purse strings IS Dad'?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft structure '握ってんのは〜だ' presents 'the one who holds the purse strings' as a topic and identifies it as Dad. は + exhaustive identification is the standard pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が wouldn't fit the nominalized topic slot cleanly here. を can't mark a nominalized subject.

contrast_examples.en: The one who decides is the father. [cleft identification]
The father decides. [neutral]

prompt.context_jp: 誰が お前の結婚式の 心配なんかするか / 俺___結婚式だ
prompt.prompt_en: Yasuo reveals it's HIS own wedding, not his daughter's. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: '俺の結婚式だ' uses の as a possessive — 'it's MY wedding (not yours)'. The contrast is lexical (俺 vs お前), not particle-level.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺は結婚式だ would awkwardly mean 'as for me, it's a wedding'. 俺が結婚式だ is ungrammatical as 俺 can't equal 結婚式 directly.

contrast_examples.en: It's MY wedding.
I'm the one getting married. [exhaustive が]

prompt.context_jp: みちるの言葉に、桑野は返事の代わりに小さく舌を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes the idiom meaning 'clicked his tongue (in annoyance)'?

feedback.correct_en: 舌を打つ is the set phrase for a small tongue-click of annoyance — exactly Kuwano's reaction to being corrected.
feedback.incorrect_en: 舌を叩く isn't idiomatic. 舌を鳴らす exists but usually describes a louder, more deliberate sound — not the 'small' click 小さく舌を打つ captures.

contrast_examples.en: He clicked his tongue — tsk.
To smack one's lips (enjoying food). [different idiom]

prompt.context_jp: ___も積もれば山となるとはよく言ったもので、親戚たちの小さな一言一言が、
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the proverb 'many small things add up to something big'?

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる is the fixed proverb — 'even dust, piled up, becomes a mountain'. It captures how small remarks accumulate into real weight.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 and 水 aren't part of this proverb. Though logically close, Japanese fixes the image to 塵 (dust).

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Dust piled up becomes a mountain. [set proverb]

contrast_examples.jp: 小さな積み重ねが大事だ。
contrast_examples.en: Small accumulations matter. [paraphrase]

prompt.context_jp: いちいち ___たたかないと 診察 受けられないんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'say nasty/insulting things'?

feedback.correct_en: 憎まれ口をたたく is the set collocation for making deliberately provocative, snarky remarks — exactly Natsumi's characterization of Shinsuke's banter.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悪口を言う and 文句を言う exist but don't pair with たたく. The verb たたく specifically collocates with 憎まれ口 or 軽口.

contrast_examples.en: To make snarky remarks. [collocation with たたく]
To speak ill. [different verb pairing]

prompt.context_jp: そんな言い方したら ___も___もない
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase means 'that's too blunt / that kills it'?

feedback.correct_en: 身も蓋もない means saying something so bluntly there's no nuance left — exactly Yasuo's objection to Shinsuke's too-honest framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元も子もない means 'losing everything (gain and principal)' — about failed results, not blunt speech. 何もかもない isn't a set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: それじゃ身も蓋もない。
contrast_examples.en: That's too blunt. [no nuance left]

contrast_examples.jp: 失敗したら元も子もない。
contrast_examples.en: If you fail, you lose everything. [different idiom]

prompt.context_jp: 夏美のヤツ 全く ___ 持ちません
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'refuses to listen at all'?

feedback.correct_en: 聞く耳を持たない is the fixed idiom for 'won't listen / refuses to hear'. Shinsuke reports Natsumi 'has no ear to listen'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 聞く気がない exists but takes が, not を持つ. 聞く力 isn't idiomatic in this sense.

contrast_examples.en: Won't listen at all. [set idiom]
Has no intention to listen. [similar meaning, different structure]

prompt.context_jp: あの___にして この___あり
prompt.prompt_jp: あの___にして この娘あり
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the saying meaning 'like father, like daughter'.

feedback.correct_en: The classical pattern この父にしてこの子あり means 'such a father, such a child'. Shinsuke twists it for Natsumi and her father.
feedback.incorrect_en: 親 or 人 would break the fixed rhetorical pattern that requires the specific parent-child pairing 父〜娘 (or 子).

contrast_examples.jp: この父にしてこの子あり。
contrast_examples.en: Like father, like child. [classical saying]
A frog's child is a frog. [similar proverb]

prompt.context_jp: ___ないで 教えてくださいよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'don't be coy / don't make me wait'?

feedback.correct_en: もったいつける means to deliberately make something seem important or hold back dramatically — exactly what Shinsuke is doing with the secret.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気取らないで means 'don't put on airs' — different nuance. 隠さないで ('don't hide it') is close but loses the 'teasing / drawing it out' nuance of もったいつける.

contrast_examples.jp: もったいつけないで教えて。
contrast_examples.en: Stop being coy and tell me.
Don't hide it, tell me. [similar but plainer]

prompt.context_jp: 水分___を忘れない そうやって解消するしかないですね
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the phrase 'staying hydrated'?

feedback.correct_en: 水分補給 is the standard medical/health collocation for hydration — the doctor's set advice vocabulary.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水分補充 is understandable but much rarer and sounds mechanical. 水分供給 would mean 'supplying water (to something)', not drinking it.

contrast_examples.jp: こまめに水分補給してください。
contrast_examples.en: Stay hydrated frequently. [standard health advice]
Refill fuel. [補充 for tanks/stock]

prompt.context_jp: 信介が夏美を呼び出そうとする場面。「何のために？」と聞かれて。
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for Shinsuke's slightly defensive, blunt style?

choices.text: 会うのに理由が必要ですか？
会うために理由を必要としますか？
会うことには理由が要りますか？

feedback.correct_en: 会うのに理由が必要ですか？ — the のに ('for the purpose of') + 必要 pattern is the natural, slightly clipped way to push back. Matches Shinsuke's voice exactly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly literal/translationese. C is grammatical but feels stiffer and less idiomatic than のに+必要 in spoken Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 話すのに準備が必要ですか？
contrast_examples.en: Do you need prep to talk? [same のに+必要 pattern]

contrast_examples.jp: 話すために準備を必要としますか？
contrast_examples.en: [grammatical but stilted]

prompt.context_jp: 夏美がつぶやく場面。「男って…」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Natsumi's casual lament about men?

choices.text: 男って どいつもこいつも どうして素直じゃないのかなぁ
男性は全員 なぜ素直ではないのでしょうか
男たちはみんな どうして素直じゃないですか

feedback.correct_en: どいつもこいつも + のかなぁ gives the exasperated, casual grumble that fits Natsumi in a private moment with Michiru.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is formal/written-register and clashes with the intimate scene. C mixes casual 'みんな' with a strange ですか question that sounds unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 男ってどいつもこいつも…
contrast_examples.en: Men — every single one of them... [casual exasperation]

contrast_examples.jp: 男性は皆、なぜ素直ではないのでしょう。
contrast_examples.en: Why aren't men honest? [formal/essay tone]

prompt.context_jp: 信介が金魚に向かって独り言を言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as sarcastic Shinsuke-style grumbling about marriage?

choices.text: 結婚なんかしてみろ 気は遣うし 水は汚されるし 酸素も半分だ
結婚をするとしたら 気を遣い 水が汚染され 酸素が半減する
結婚してみたら 気を遣って 水が汚くなって 酸素も少ない

feedback.correct_en: The command-form conditional してみろ + rapid 〜し 〜し 〜だ listing gives the dismissive, rhythmic rant that fits Shinsuke's voice.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is technical/written and loses the sarcastic bite. C is grammatical but flat — it lacks the 'go ahead and try it, see what happens' challenge of してみろ.

contrast_examples.en: Just try it — it's awful. [challenging してみろ]
If you do it, it's awful. [neutral conditional]

prompt.context_jp: 親戚のおじさんが信介に説教する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a nagging relative's lecture?

choices.text: 相手が再婚じゃヤダなんて 言ってる立場じゃないのも 分かってんだろう？
相手が再婚であることを拒否する立場にないことも理解しているはずだ
相手が再婚ならイヤだと言う立場でないと分かるでしょう

feedback.correct_en: 〜なんて言ってる立場じゃない + 分かってんだろう is the classic nagging-uncle register — colloquial contractions and quoted complaint.
feedback.incorrect_en: B reads like a legal document. C is grammatical but reads as neutral exposition, missing the 分かってんだろう pressure tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 文句言ってる立場じゃないだろう。
contrast_examples.en: You're not in a position to complain. [nagging register]

contrast_examples.jp: 文句を言う立場にない。
contrast_examples.en: Not in a position to complain. [formal/written]

prompt.context_jp: 疲れ切った夏美がみちるの家に突然現れる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for an exhausted, 'please just let me crash' request?

choices.text: 何も聞かないで 今夜泊めて
何も質問しないで 今夜宿泊させて
何も聞かずに 今夜泊まらせてくれますか

feedback.correct_en: Short imperative 泊めて with 何も聞かないで captures the raw, intimate exhaustion — dropping politeness entirely with a close friend.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses stiff vocabulary (質問・宿泊) that feels like hotel paperwork. C's くれますか politeness creates an awkward distance for someone collapsing at a friend's door.

contrast_examples.jp: 何も聞かないで。泊めて。
contrast_examples.en: Don't ask — just let me stay. [close, raw]

contrast_examples.jp: 宿泊させていただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: May I stay the night? [hotel-formal]
